item.title: LUNAR ECLIPSE TONIGHT
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: You won't need special glasses to see the lunar eclipse coming to Pensacola tonight. While Florida residents won't see a total lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow — known as the umbra — will cover almost 94% of the moon. You'll have to stay up late if you want to see the peak of the eclipse, which will happen shortly before midnight, but most people…
item.content:encoded: You won't need special glasses to see the lunar eclipse coming to Pensacola tonight. While Florida residents won't see a total lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow — known as the umbra — will cover almost 94% of the moon. You'll have to stay up late if you want to see the peak of the eclipse, which will happen shortly before midnight, but most people should be able to see the start of the eclipse earlier in the evening. Of course, the best viewing will be away from lights and with no clouds. The eclipse begins: 8:23 p.m. tonight with the maximum at 11:12pm and ending around 2am.

item.title: FORMER LIBRARY BECOMES CHILD CARE CENTER
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: For nearly 50 years, a building on North A Street sat empty — once Pensacola's first library for the Black community, shut down back in 1976. Now it's open again, this time as a childcare center. The city celebrated the official opening of the Alice S. Williams Center this week. It's named for Alice Strudivant Williams, who founded the first night…
item.content:encoded: For nearly 50 years, a building on North A Street sat empty — once Pensacola's first library for the Black community, shut down back in 1976. Now it's open again, this time as a childcare center. The city celebrated the official opening of the Alice S. Williams Center this week. It's named for Alice Strudivant Williams, who founded the first night school for African Americans in Pensacola. The center will serve infants up to two years old. Mayor D-C Reeves says preserving the building had been talked about for years. The project got 500-thousand dollars from a state African American cultural and historical grant, plus 300-thousand dollars from the Community Redevelopment Agency.

item.content:encoded: Florida’s four-month Hunting, Fishing and Camping sales-tax holiday kicks off Tuesday, Sept. 1, and runs through Dec. 31. Shoppers can skip sales tax on camping and hunting gear — including guns and ammunition — with no price cap on firearms, bows or accessories. The holiday is part of the state’s tax package signed with the new budget and is expected to save shoppers millions statewide.

item.title: Grand Jury: DeSantis Administration Misappropriated $10 Million
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: In a sealed report, a Florida state grand jury found that the DeSantis administration misappropriated $10 million in taxpayer money by diverting funds from a Medicaid settlement to the Hope Florida Foundation, as reported from CBS News Miami. State Representative Alex Andrade of Pensacola first raised the alarm — and a grand jury is backing him…
item.content:encoded: In a sealed report, a Florida state grand jury found that the DeSantis administration misappropriated $10 million in taxpayer money by diverting funds from a Medicaid settlement to the Hope Florida Foundation, as reported from CBS News Miami. State Representative Alex Andrade of Pensacola first raised the alarm — and a grand jury is backing him up. The panel says 10 million dollars from a Medicaid settlement was misappropriated into the Hope Florida Foundation in 2025, then moved within days to the Republican Party and two political action committees. The target: defeating a ballot measure to legalize recreational marijuana. One of those PACs was chaired by James Uthmeier — then the governor's general counsel, now Florida's attorney general.

item.content:encoded: The City of Milton is bringing back its free Bands on the Blackwater concert series this fall. Live music will be featured along the Blackwater River every Friday night from September 4 through October 30, from 7 to 9 p.m. The lineup includes Vinyl Revival, Box of Rox, Hired Guns, Midlife Crisis L.A., Symphonic Thunder, Bone Dry Band, Blackwater Country and The Modern Elderados. Concertgoers can bring lawn chairs or blankets and enjoy live music, food vendors and the downtown riverfront. On September 11, a special 9/11 remembrance will begin at 6:45 p.m.

He first joined the Century Town Council in 2017 and became interim mayor in 2023 following the resignation of Ben Boutwell. Gomez was later elected mayor without…
item.content:encoded: The Town of Century is remembering former Mayor and Councilman Luis Gomez Jr., who died recently at the age of 64. The town honored Gomez during Tuesday night’s council meeting. He first joined the Century Town Council in 2017 and became interim mayor in 2023 following the resignation of Ben Boutwell. Gomez was later elected mayor without opposition in a special election and again in 2024. Council President Dynette Lewis praised Gomez’s passion for Century, while Councilman John Bass recalled that even when Gomez was feeling ill, he remained focused on the town and its progress.

The money will help provide financial assistance to local families dealing with a childhood cancer diagnosis, while also supporting research into safer treatments and…
item.content:encoded: Sandy Sansing Dealerships is donating $100,000 to the Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research Gulf Coast. The donation was presented Tuesday at Sandy Sansing BMW in Pensacola. The money will help provide financial assistance to local families dealing with a childhood cancer diagnosis, while also supporting research into safer treatments and potential cures. Sandy Sansing says the dealership is proud to support Rally and families across the Gulf Coast. The donation continues a partnership focused on helping children and families today while investing in research that could improve treatment options in the future.

item.dc:creator: news6334

Commission Chairman Colten Wright addressed rumors head-on, saying there was no vote planned despite online chatter. The topic wasn't…
item.content:encoded: About 25 people signed up to speak at Tuesday's County Commission Committee of the Whole meeting — most of them opposing a proposed boardwalk and event center on the east side of the Navarre Beach Causeway Bridge. Commission Chairman Colten Wright addressed rumors head-on, saying there was no vote planned despite online chatter. The topic wasn't on the agenda, and no vote could have been taken either way. The project's back in the spotlight because it's now out to bid — contractors have until September 3rd to respond. A Change-dot-org petition against the project had drawn nearly four-thousand signatures by meeting time.

item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Gulf Winds Credit Union says it will operate under a new name and identity: TruWorth Credit Union. The rebrand is expected to take effect in spring 2027. Gulf Winds also announced plans to acquire Madison County Community Bank in Madison, Florida. The deal would add about 200 million dollars in assets and two branches in Madison and Perry,…
item.content:encoded: Gulf Winds Credit Union says it will operate under a new name and identity: TruWorth Credit Union. The rebrand is expected to take effect in spring 2027. Gulf Winds also announced plans to acquire Madison County Community Bank in Madison, Florida. The deal would add about 200 million dollars in assets and two branches in Madison and Perry, bringing the combined organization to more than one-point-seven billion dollars in assets and 15 locations across Florida and Alabama. The credit union says the combined organization would serve more than 87-thousand members. The transaction still requires shareholder and regulatory approval, with final approval expected in mid-2027.

Assistant State Attorney Greg Marcille says Keyunta Ewing will be transferred to adult court, with formal charges to be determined. Ewing surrendered Friday in connection with the August 13th shooting that killed 20-something Adarius Odom and…
item.content:encoded: A 16-year-old Century teen charged in the deadly shooting at Showalter Park will be tried as an adult. Assistant State Attorney Greg Marcille says Keyunta Ewing will be transferred to adult court, with formal charges to be determined. Ewing surrendered Friday in connection with the August 13th shooting that killed 20-something Adarius Odom and wounded another man. Investigators say witnesses identified Ewing as the shooter and told deputies he demanded money before firing several shots at Odom. Ewing had initially told investigators he was at the park to watch a fistfight.

item.content:encoded: Republican gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds has picked his running mate. Donalds named state Senator Bryan Avila as his choice for lieutenant governor Tuesday, making the announcement at Miami's Freedom Tower. Avila, a Republican from Miami Springs, is a captain in the Florida Army National Guard who's represented Cuban-majority communities in both chambers of the legislature. Accepting the nomination, Avila invoked his family's story, saying his parents fled communist Cuba for freedom in Florida — and vowing that under a Donalds administration, socialism will never find a home in the state.

item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Florida is moving to drop four vaccine requirements for students in public and private schools. The state Department of Health wants to eliminate school-entry mandates for Hepatitis B, chickenpox, HIB, and pneumococcal disease — for children from pre-K through 12th grade. It's part of Surgeon General Doctor Joseph Ladapo's push, announced nearly a…
item.content:encoded: Florida is moving to drop four vaccine requirements for students in public and private schools. The state Department of Health wants to eliminate school-entry mandates for Hepatitis B, chickenpox, HIB, and pneumococcal disease — for children from pre-K through 12th grade. It's part of Surgeon General Doctor Joseph Ladapo's push, announced nearly a year ago, to end vaccine mandates statewide. Some doctors are raising concerns. The Department of Health has opened a 21-day public comment period before deciding whether to finalize the rule.

The state average for regular unleaded gasoline is $3.86 per gallon, about the same as a week ago. Meanwhile, the national average edged slightly higher over the past week, rising from $4.07 to $4.10 per gallon. In the Escambia County area, the average is the…
item.content:encoded: Florida gas prices remain relatively stable, despite rising oil and gasoline futures. The state average for regular unleaded gasoline is $3.86 per gallon, about the same as a week ago. Meanwhile, the national average edged slightly higher over the past week, rising from $4.07 to $4.10 per gallon. In the Escambia County area, the average is the lowest in the state at $3.76, In Santa Rosa, the average is $3.79.

item.title: ESCAMBIA SCHOOLS USE WEATHERSTEM FOR WEATHER
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Thousands packed stadiums across the region Friday for opening night of high school football — but storms nearly stole the show. Tate and Pine Forest both saw delays under a severe thunderstorm watch. Every athletic trainer was watching WeatherSTEM, a Tallahassee-based tracking system with stations at all seven Escambia County high schools. The…
item.content:encoded: Thousands packed stadiums across the region Friday for opening night of high school football — but storms nearly stole the show. Tate and Pine Forest both saw delays under a severe thunderstorm watch. Every athletic trainer was watching WeatherSTEM, a Tallahassee-based tracking system with stations at all seven Escambia County high schools. The system's color-coded like beach flags — lightning inside ten miles clears the field; beyond 30, it's all clear.

item.title: LAWMAKERS, MILITARY LEADERS MEET TO TACKLE 98 CONGESTION.
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: State and military leaders are weighing their options for easing Highway 98 congestion by Hurlburt Field, after past fixes -- like the flyover near the base entrance -- haven't solved the problem. Congressman Jimmy Patronis has filed the Warrior Road Act, aiming to make security-critical infrastructure projects a federal funding priority. Senator…
item.content:encoded: State and military leaders are weighing their options for easing Highway 98 congestion by Hurlburt Field, after past fixes -- like the flyover near the base entrance -- haven't solved the problem. Congressman Jimmy Patronis has filed the Warrior Road Act, aiming to make security-critical infrastructure projects a federal funding priority. Senator Gaetz says solving the congestion ultimately comes down to two things -- land, and money. The main concern is keeping the base and the missions they support in Northwest Florida. In the meantime, the base has requested additional Florida troopers to be in the area helping with traffic.
